name: Strata 0.2.8
body: # Strata 0.2.8: faster Arc B-series pairs and four-card Radeon servers, a Mac DeepSeek memory leak fixed, fewer lost tool calls The app is 0.2.8. Control and every engine package are 0.1.54. ## The numbers first - **Two Intel Arc Pro B65 cards: decode 17% to 23% faster, prompts about 7% to 13% faster.** Chat runs at 71 to 74 tokens per second, against 60 to 63 before, and JSON at 80 to 83, against 67 to 68. We tested two Arc Pro B65 32 GB cards with Qwen3.8-Flash-Next IQ3_S, five paired runs, and every pair was faster. The answers are the same as before. This applies to exactly two Arc B-series cards; one card, A-series cards and three or more cards run as before. - **Four Radeon AI PRO R9700 cards serving many requests: 2.4 times the total speed at 32 requests at once** (155 to 370 tokens per second in total; at 8 at once, 157 to 261). One request alone runs at the same speed as before (67 tokens per second). Setup and the launcher pick this for exactly four R9700 cards running Qwen3.8 IQ3_S. All 32 answers matched a single-request run, and two soaks (25 and 12 minutes, 1,600 requests) had no errors. - **DeepSeek on the Mac no longer slows down after a few requests.** On the Metal engine every request left about 1.3 GB of GPU buffers behind, until the Mac ran short of memory and decode fell from 16 tokens per second to 3. Memory now stays flat at 76 GB over 34 requests, and decode stays at 18 to 22 tokens per second, with the same answers. Tested on an M5 Max with 128 GB, not on a 256 GB Mac Studio. - **Tool calls the model writes slightly wrong now still go through, by default.** Over 1,462 agent turns, 98.3% are now read as intended, against 92.9% before. This only applies to tools the request declared. - **RTX cards with 12 GB or less: the 0.2.7 routing speed-up is off again by default.** It made answers faster (RTX 3060: story +15%, code +37%), but your reports and our own checks tied it to repeated text in long sessions. With nothing set, the engine now routes exactly as 0.2.6 did. To get the speed back, turn on "Faster answers on 12 GB NVIDIA cards" under Models, Native engine settings, Speed (or run `strata launch --set STRATA_ROUTE_PRIOR=1.5`). - **DeepSeek no longer stops in the middle of a word.** The server ended a reply on pieces such as `im`, `|` or `>`, so "Nerazim" came out as "Neraz" (#4576, #4137). It happened when a DeepSeek server was started from a config that did not name the model family. - **0.2.8 against 0.2.7.1, five paired runs each.** On one RTX A6000 with Qwen IQ3_S, decode went from 105.9 to 111.4 tokens per second on a story and from 139.8 to 145.2 on code; prompts are unchanged (1,927 and 1,924 at 4K, 2,571 and 2,569 at 20K). On one Radeon R9700, decode went from 73.7 to 79.7 on a story and from 106.3 to 107.8 on code; prompts are within 0.4% once the engine is warm. DeepSeek 2.25 decode is 4.3% faster on an RTX A6000, with the same output as 0.2.7.1 on our score check. ## What is new - **Arc B-series pairs.** The first card starts the next window while the second card is still checking the current one (`--pipeline-windows 2`), and setup writes `--spec 2` for the pair. Turn it off with `--pipeline-windows 0`; a `--spec` you set yourself is kept. The Arc engine also reads prompts about 5% faster on B-series cards with a new attention path, and three bugs that stopped `--pipeline-windows` from running at all are fixed. - **Four-card Radeon profile.** For four R9700 cards: 32 request slots in 4 groups, layer split 13,26,39, a prompt chunk of 2048 and three small switches. It only fills in what you have not set. Turn it off with `"four_card_profile": false` in the config. - **Bigger batch windows on AMD.** The HIP engines now check and batch up to 16 rows at once instead of 8, which is what the four-card profile needs. The answers are bit for bit those of the 8-row build on every card we ran (10 of 10 on R9700, RTX PRO 5000, A6000, A4000 and P100). NVIDIA, Intel and Mac builds stay at 8. - **DeepSeek prompt speed, opt-in.** `DS4_FAT_ROWS` (thanks to lyesrock, PR #4366) gives the busiest experts of a long prompt one bigger matrix multiply: +2% to +5% on two RTX A6000. It is off by default, because the gain is under our bar for a default and the output is not bit-exact. - **A clearer message on Arc and older CPUs.** A model folder without `native_experts.txt` is read as the AVX-512 pack, and the engine used to blame the CPU. It now names the real cause, and `strata doctor` warns before the start. - **One source for the driver floor.** Setup now reads the CUDA 12 driver floor from the engine package, so setup and the update agree. The floor itself has not changed: 575.51, or 576.02 on Windows. ## Fixed, from your reports - **App:** - DeepSeek no longer fails to load with picture reading off (#4358, #4359, #4505, #4507). The app now sends DeepSeek only the options it takes, and "GPU memory for other apps" goes out as `--reserve-mib` (#4504). - The wait for a big model to load now follows the model size, as `strata launch` does (#4191, #3459; thanks to miketgv, PR #3817). - "See engine log" no longer points at a log that was never written (#3714). - **Monitor:** with a model running, an AMD card on Windows showed load, memory and temperature as "Not available". The Monitor now fills in what the engine does not report, and reads the temperature on Windows AMD cards (#3727). On Linux, a server's remote-console chip no longer shows up as a graphics card. - **Terminal and setup:** - The update's test start skips DeepSeek configs (#4440; thanks to ai-bits, PR #4267). - A saved lower-case model tag such as `iq3_xxs` is found (#4209, PR #4317). - The packaged Terminal runs setup without `CMakeLists.txt`, and `strata install --source modelscope` passes its options on (#4188). - **Memory and cache:** - A 256K start on two cards no longer takes the Strix Halo reserve off the RAM store. On 2x A6000 the RAM store grew from 77.7 to 106.5 GB (#4147). - The conversation cache no longer runs short when the PLE table is locked (#4518). - Parking an idle `--batch` slot keeps the shared prefix, so the first token of round 2 takes 0.66 s instead of 3.3 s (#4420). - The automatic expert cache leaves the reserve you asked for (#4474). - A new engine waits for the old one to give its memory back (#4051). - **Tool calls and the server:** - An argument that quotes a tool call stays exact (#4078; thanks to Tsury, PR #4132). - Damaged arguments, a missing `` and a stray closing think tag no longer lose the call (#4427, #4077). - **DeepSeek on several cards:** - A layer split's chunked prompt no longer deadlocks (PR #4211). - `slot_load()` writes each tensor-parallel member's state under its own device (#4350; the single-card fault is still open). - **Mac:** the DeepSeek memory leak described above. ## Going back to 0.2.7.1 `strata components rollback` returns to the previous engine. The Qwen route prior and tool-call recovery can both be set the 0.2.7 way: `STRATA_ROUTE_PRIOR=1.5` and `"tool_call_recovery": false` in the model's run config. The 16-row windows are a build option (`-DSTRATA_WINDOW_MAX_T=8`); there is no switch at run time. ## Off unless you turn it on - `DS4_FAT_ROWS=N` (DeepSeek, CUDA). - Everything listed under "Off unless you turn it on" in 0.2.7 is unchanged. ## What we did not test - A 256 GB Mac Studio, or any Mac other than one M5 Max. - The four-card profile on anything other than four R9700 cards, and 64 slots at long context. - The Monitor fix on a Windows AMD graphics card. We tested it on Linux AMD cards and on Windows with NVIDIA and an AMD integrated GPU. If you have a Radeon on Windows, please tell us whether the Monitor now shows load, memory and temperature. - The Windows commit-limit side of #4518, the full #4051 wedge on a host with little RAM, and #4427 on a real model beyond the parser tests. - Metal and SYCL builds with 16-row windows; they stay at 8 and were only compile-checked. - The B-series pipeline on anything other than two Arc Pro B65 cards. - Strix Halo changes are not in this release. ## Updating - **App:** the in-app update offers 0.2.8, or download the installer below. - **Terminal:** run `strata update`. It fetches Control 0.1.54 and the 0.1.54 engine in the same run, and keeps the old engine for `strata components rollback`. If your Terminal is older than 0.2.0 (for example 0.1.45.x), run the install line again. - **DeepSeek engine:** it updates itself on the next `strata launch`. - **DGX Spark:** run `strata update`; it reads `strata-feed-linux-aarch64.json`. - **Mac:** the app, the Terminal and the DeepSeek engine are signed and notarized. ## Downloads 40 files. Three installers (Windows, Linux AppImage, Mac dmg) and the Mac updater archive `Strata.app.tar.gz` (0.2.8), with the update signatures for the Windows, Linux and Mac app; the four Control packages (0.1.54: Windows, Linux x86, Mac, Linux ARM64); 14 Qwen engine packages (0.1.54: Windows CUDA 13, CUDA 12 and three AMD packages; Linux CUDA 13, CUDA 12, four AMD packages and Intel SYCL; Mac Metal; Linux ARM64); six DeepSeek engine packages (0.1.54: Windows CUDA 13 and AMD RDNA3, Linux CUDA 13 and AMD rx9070, Mac Metal, Linux ARM64); `strata-feed.json` and `strata-feed-linux-aarch64.json` with their signatures; `latest.json`, `install-manifest.txt`, `install.sh`, `install.ps1` and `SHA256SUMS.txt`. The DeepSeek CUDA packages are built for sm_86, sm_89 and sm_120. --- Strata is free and open source. If it runs well on your PC, a coffee keeps the work on it going:

name: Strata 0.2.7.1: NVIDIA DGX Spark and DeepSeek on the Mac
body:
# Strata 0.2.7: faster 12 GB NVIDIA cards, DeepSeek on Ryzen AI Max, a bigger web chat page, French

The app is 0.2.7. The 0.2.7.1 section below is the new part of this release; everything after it is the 0.2.7 text. Control is 0.1.53 since 0.2.7.1. The engine packages of 0.2.7 stay at 0.1.52, and the new Spark engines are 0.1.53.

## 0.2.7.1: NVIDIA DGX Spark, and DeepSeek on the Mac

This update adds two things: Strata now runs on the NVIDIA DGX Spark (Linux ARM64), and DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash runs on Apple silicon Macs. **If you use Windows, Linux with an x86 processor, or a Mac for Qwen only, you get no new engine, no speed change and no app change, and you do not need to update.** Your Terminal will still show a small update (Control 0.1.52 to 0.1.53). It brings a reader for the update feed that skips entries it does not understand instead of stopping, so a later release can add a new kind of computer without breaking yours. Your engines stay as they are.

### DGX Spark

- **What runs.** Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (IQ3_S and the NVFP4 pack, 64K context) and DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash 2.00 bpw. We tested one Spark (Ubuntu 24.04, NVIDIA driver 580, CUDA 13.0). We do not know that it works on any other ARM computer. The Spark needs glibc 2.39 or newer (Ubuntu 24.04, DGX OS 7) and driver 580.65 or newer.
- **Install.** The Terminal only, because there is no desktop app for ARM Linux:

  ```sh
  curl -fsSL https://github.com/Niko1221/Strata/releases/latest/download/install.sh -o install.sh && sh install.sh
  strata launch
  ```

  `strata launch` downloads the Spark engine, shows what each model needs, and starts the one you pick. The guide is [docs/DGX_SPARK_LINUX.md](https://github.com/Niko1221/Strata/blob/main/docs/DGX_SPARK_LINUX.md).
- **Speed.** Four Spark settings are on by default. The table is the same engine with them on and with them off (`STRATA_SM121_PERF=0`), on one Spark with 64K context and 256-token answers, medians of four runs per cell. It is not a comparison with 0.2.7 or with another machine.

  | Model | Settings | Prompt, tok/s (4K / 16K / 32K) | Answer, tok/s (4K / 16K / 32K) |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | IQ3_S | on | 1,296 / 1,680 / 1,735 | 45.5 / 46.5 / 46.5 |
  | IQ3_S | off | 1,203 / 1,416 / 1,276 | 48.5 / 45.3 / 45.2 |
  | NVFP4 | on | 1,408 / 1,670 / 1,698 | 42.8 / 40.5 / 40.1 |
  | NVFP4 | off | 1,156 / 1,350 / 1,353 | 41.0 / 41.2 / 38.4 |

  Prompts are 1.20 times faster on IQ3_S (90% range 1.12 to 1.31) and 1.24 times faster on NVFP4 (1.14 to 1.36). Answer speed did not change in this check: 0.996 times on IQ3_S (0.97 to 1.02, and 0.94 times at 4K) and 1.02 times on NVFP4 (1.00 to 1.05). An earlier run had shown about 5% for each of two answer-speed settings; this check did not repeat it.
- **Several chats at once.** `strata launch` sets four slots on a Spark. With IQ3_S, 2,000-token prompts and 128-token answers, all clients at the same time, the total over all clients was 35.6 tok/s for 8 clients, 41.7 for 16 and 47.3 for 32 at four slots, and 54.2 for 32 clients at eight slots. One chat alone answers at about 46 tok/s, so several chats mostly share the Spark's speed. We also gave every client its own prompt and a hidden code: each answer named its own code and nobody else's (8 clients on four slots, 16 clients on eight slots), and none failed or hung.
- **Answer quality.** The faster prompt path rounds numbers a little differently, so the same question can come back in different words. On a 61-task suite (finding facts in long documents, copying up to 72 exact rows, summaries, code, JSON, agent loops with tools) the settings on passed 56 tasks and off 51 on IQ3_S, and 56 against 52 on NVFP4. Every run found all 63 facts, and no agent loop made an invalid tool call. The answers differ in wording on 21 of the 61 tasks (IQ3_S) and 25 (NVFP4), and the wins and losses go both ways. Read it as no loss that we could measure, not as an improvement. On NVFP4 one 40-row register lost a row with the settings on (616 of 642 extraction facts against 621). To get the answers of 0.2.7 back on the Spark, set `STRATA_SM121_PERF=0`.
- **DeepSeek on the Spark.** DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash 2.00 bpw at 8K context in the default Faster mode (5 of 6 experts per word) answered a short chat at 13 to 18 tok/s, and the first answer after a start is the slowest. With `--experts 6` the first run measured 17 to 23 tok/s on a 1.7K-token chat.
- **What we did not test.** DeepSeek beyond short chats, contexts above 128K, a long soak, and reading pictures (it is built in and was not tried). The Q2_0 and Gyro packs do not start on ARM, because their CPU kernels exist for x86 only. There is no desktop app, HIP, SYCL or CPU-only engine for ARM. `strata doctor --live` lists the GB10 without a memory figure, because `nvidia-smi` reports none for it.
- **Thanks.** @ferstar's pull request #3622 made the engine build for ARM64 and is the base of this port; their name is on the commit.

### DeepSeek on the Mac

- **What runs.** DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash 2.00 bpw and 2.25 bpw on Apple silicon (M1 or newer, macOS 15 or newer), text only. `strata launch` fetches the DeepSeek engine for the Mac the first time you pick DeepSeek, like on Windows. It needs 257 GB (2.00) or 274 GB (2.25) of free disk on the internal SSD or an NVMe drive, not a USB or network drive. We recommend 64 GB of memory or more, but we tested one Mac only, an M5 Max with 128 GB. A Mac with less memory starts, and setup says it will be much slower and asks before it goes on, but we ran nothing under 128 GB.
- **Install.** Use the Terminal (the app is still 0.2.7 and we did not try DeepSeek on the Mac in it):

  ```sh
  strata launch --family deepseek41 --model ist-das-2.00bpw --plan
  strata launch --family deepseek41 --model ist-das-2.00bpw
  ```

  The guide is [docs/DEEPSEEK_MAC.md](https://github.com/Niko1221/Strata/blob/main/docs/DEEPSEEK_MAC.md).
- **Speed.** Measured on the M5 Max with 128 GB, the engine as shipped, one fresh start per run, two runs each, in tokens per second. They were measured while another person's Qwen server (a 60 GB model, loaded and idle) was running on the same Mac, so both shared the file cache. A Mac with nothing else running may be faster; we did not measure that.

  | | 2.00 bpw | 2.25 bpw |
  |---|---|---|
  | Short answer, code prompt | 15.2 to 16.0 | 14.7 to 15.3 |
  | Short answer, agent prompt | 15.3 to 16.2 | 13.1 to 13.6 |
  | Answer after a 3,000-token prompt | 14.5 to 15.1 | 11.7 to 11.8 |
  | Answer after a 14,000-token prompt | 13.8 to 15.1 | 10.5 to 11.1 |
  | Reading a 3,000-token prompt | 236 to 241 | 293 to 294 |
  | Reading a 14,000-token prompt | 479 to 512 | 553 to 586 |
  | Reading a 32,000-token prompt | 609 | 720 |

  The model does not fit in memory, so part of it is read from the SSD for every word (48 MB per word on 2.00, 111 MB on 2.25). Answer speed is limited by those reads and by the processor, not by the graphics chip.
- **Quality.** The 2.25 set stays closer to the original model: on a scoring run over 4,995 text positions it ends about 8% above the original model's perplexity, and the 2.00 set about 17% above. The Mac's closeness score for 2.25 (0.111, lower is closer) sits inside the run-to-run spread of the same set on a Radeon AI PRO R9700 (0.109 to 0.111). A hidden code in a long text was found at 14,600, 17,000, 19,500 and 26,200 tokens.
- **A choice we made.** The Mac reads DeepSeek's large per-word table (the Engram) with two threads. With more threads, 3 to 9 of 16 runs gave slightly different words from the same prompt. We have not found the cause. Two threads cost about 3 to 12% of prompt speed (about 12% at 3,000 tokens, 7 to 12% at 14,000, about 3% at 32,000) and do not change answer speed. `DS4_ENGRAM_THREADS=N` sets another number. Two runs of the same prompt can still differ in the last digits of a score, because the engine moves experts between memory and the SSD as it learns what the prompt needs; the answers stay equally good.
- **Found and fixed in testing, before release.** A code hidden past 16,000 tokens was missed, and some short follow-up turns went wrong.
- **What we did not test.** Any Mac with less than 128 GB, prompts longer than about 32,000 tokens, and the 1.75 bpw set (not offered on the Mac). There are no pictures yet, because DeepSeek's picture reader was not run on the Metal engine, and a picture sent to a DeepSeek model on a Mac is refused. The DSpark drafter is off on the Mac, because it gave the same answers and no speed-up. Qwen on the Mac keeps its pictures.

## What you will notice

- **NVIDIA cards with 12 GB or less answer faster.** The router now prefers experts that are already on the card, which saves page-ins from RAM. On an RTX 3060 12 GB (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next IQ3_XXS, five paired runs against the same build with the setting off), a story answer went from 46.2 to 53.1 tok/s (+15%) and a code answer from 45.7 to 62.5 tok/s (+37%). It picks a slightly different set of experts, so the wording of answers changes. We checked the answers on that card (IQ3_XXS) with 80 tasks and saw no copy or code errors. Agent loops may finish slightly less often, within the run-to-run spread: out of 10 agent tasks, 4.5 passed on average over 4 runs at 1.5, against 5.6 over 7 runs with the setting off, where the off runs alone ranged from 4 to 6. A stronger setting (2.0) did show copy and code defects, so the default is 1.5. It applies to a discrete NVIDIA card of 13 GiB or less; larger cards, Radeon and Strix Halo are not changed. Off: the row "Faster answers on 12 GB NVIDIA cards" in the Expert settings (Models, Native engine settings, Speed), or `STRATA_ROUTE_PRIOR=0`.
- **Radeon RX 9000 and AI PRO R9700: faster Qwen.** Two changes: the large per-token lookup table stays in RAM when the PC has room for it, and the decode split between card and processor starts at a better value. One R9700 (32 GB) with 125 GB of RAM on Linux, Qwen IQ3_S, medians of three runs:

  | Context | Prompt before | Prompt now | Decode before | Decode now |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | 8K | 2,047 tok/s | 2,505 tok/s (+22%) | 82.9 tok/s | 94.6 tok/s (+14%) |
  | 32K | 2,491 tok/s | 2,802 tok/s (+12%) | 64.9 tok/s | 85.1 tok/s (+31%) |

  Answers can differ in wording because the work is split differently; 30 test tasks passed in every arm with no invented fact. Off: "Faster answers on Radeon RX 9000 / AI PRO R9700".
- **DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash runs on Ryzen AI Max (Strix Halo) PCs with Windows.** It has its own engine package for the gfx1151 chip, and the app or `strata launch` downloads it with the model. The new guide [docs/STRIX_HALO_WINDOWS.md](https://github.com/Niko1221/Strata/blob/main/docs/STRIX_HALO_WINDOWS.md) has the numbers and the traps, measured on a GMKtec EVO-X2 (Ryzen AI Max+ 395, 128 GB shared memory, Adrenalin 26.10.1). DeepSeek 2.00 answers a short chat at 12 to 14 tok/s and reads a 4K prompt at 214 to 234 tok/s, a 16K prompt at 326 and a 32K prompt at 342 tok/s. Those prompt rows use the word-list prompt of `tools/strata_bench.py`; ordinary prose is slower (124 to 164 tok/s on 3 to 5K-token pieces). Qwen IQ3_S on the same PC: chat 44 to 51 tok/s, 4K prompt 755, 32K prompt 792 tok/s. We measured both again on the final release package (the 4K DeepSeek prompt 229 to 234 tok/s warm, 186 to 225 on the first cold run; the Qwen prompt rows within 1%). The shared-expert stream is off by default on Windows there, because it is slower: 43.6 to 46.6 tok/s decode (+6.9%, three paired starts), same token ids. Only the 128 GB machine was tested. You need Adrenalin 26.10.1 or newer.
- **DeepSeek reads prompts faster on most PCs.** The engine no longer re-reads a batch of experts from the SSD after every prompt, picks the attention buffer size by itself and changes how the RAM store is filled. On an RTX 5070 (12 GB, 64 GB RAM, 2.25 set, three paired runs against an earlier 0.2.7 candidate): 4K prompt 116 to 170 tok/s (+47%), 8K prompt 202 to 268 tok/s (+33%). On one R9700 with the 2.25 set: 32K prompt 382 to 444 tok/s (+16%), 8K prompt 200 to 286 tok/s (+43%, but that prompt is limited by SSD reads and varies a lot between runs). The first words after a long prompt can come slower, because the store is no longer pre-filled. On the RTX 5070 a long answer still finished 8.7% sooner overall (137.5 s against 150.6 s); on one R9700 a 300-token answer after an 8K prompt took 51.9 s without the pre-fill and 48.6 s with it. `DS4_SETTLE_STORE=1` brings the pre-fill back. The speed-up switch "DeepSeek speed-ups" turns the new behaviour off in one step.
- **Four Radeon AI PRO R9700 cards run DeepSeek faster, with five experts per word by default.** With the launcher's own settings, DeepSeek 2.25: an 8K prompt 342 to 399 tok/s on the first read and 967 to 1,350 once warm (+17%, +40%), a 32K prompt 1,127 to 1,604 first and 1,183 to 1,697 warm (+42%, +43%), decode on code 88.9 to 95.0 tok/s (+7%) and on an agent task 73.5 to 79.7 (+8%). Loading takes 58 to 60 s instead of 51 s. The default is now "Faster" (5 of 6 experts per word); the quality run passed 19 of 19 tasks against 18 of 19 with six experts, and the distance to the reference model is the same (0.1102 against 0.1102). Choose Full quality in the app, or `--experts 6`, to use six.
- **DeepSeek can use 512K and 1M contexts.** Setup, the Terminal and the app offer them up to the limit of the model files, with a plain "not tested yet" note past 256K. The default stays 8K, and the app now loads a DeepSeek model with the context you chose. On an RTX 5070 a 1M context loaded in 18 s and cost about 1 GB of graphics memory, which pushed 136 experts off the card. We did not test long prompts at these sizes. The idea comes from Project Maya v1.1.28 (#442, by @needmorevram).
- **Two NVIDIA cards read long prompts much sooner on a layer split.** On a layer split over two CUDA cards the prompt is now read layer by layer in large pieces (layer-major prefill, on by default), so each layer's experts are read once per piece instead of once per 8,192 tokens. On two RTX A4000 (16 GB each, Qwen IQ3_XXS with most experts streamed from RAM, five paired runs): the first word after a 32K prompt came after 27.7 s instead of 141.8 s, after a 20K prompt after 17.5 s instead of 98.8 s, after an 8K prompt after 15.2 s instead of 41.8 s. Decode speed is the same (38.6 against 38.4 tok/s). Quality: 12 of 12 needles found with both, the quick suite passed 18 of 19 tasks in all three arms, and the first-token probabilities moved by 0.0007 to 0.009 (KL; the same top choice in every check), so wording can differ a little. If a card has no room for the bigger step, the engine reads the old way. From PR #3976 by @Norhiro, building on @vizdatom's #1670. One card, Radeon and the approximate-read mode keep the old path. Off: `STRATA_PREFILL_LAYER_MAJOR=0`; `STRATA_DEFAULTS=026` gives the old path.
- **Two NVIDIA cards share several chats faster.** On two or more NVIDIA cards with a batch of slots, the engine now runs the cards as a pipeline by default; the serial way of 0.2.1 to 0.2.6 was slower at two and four chats. Two RTX A6000 (Qwen IQ3_S, no drafting): two chats +17% (125.7 against 107.4 tok/s), four chats +22% (171.4 against 141.0). Two RTX A4000 (Q2_0 and IQ3_XXS): two chats +7 to 12%, four chats +17 to 20%, one chat 4% slower on IQ3_XXS and equal on Q2_0. Every chat still decodes exactly its own tokens. Off: `STRATA_BATCH_GROUPS_NV_SERIAL=1`, or `STRATA_DEFAULTS=026`.
- **DeepSeek reads pictures by default.** Setup and `strata launch` start DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash with the engine's own vision tower (319 MiB, no separate reader). It costs a one-time download of about 1 GB (the tower's weights, 972 MB, checked against a pinned hash) and about 1.3 GB more RAM on four R9700 (0.2 GB on one card); the graphics memory is taken from the expert cache, so the total does not grow. On four R9700 a picture question (left half red, right half blue) was answered correctly, 7.8 s for the first picture and 0.2 s once warm; on one R9700 12.7 s and 0.5 s; text requests after pictures work. The text-only answers on the agent prompt are identical with and without it; the distance to the reference model moved by +0.0014 on four R9700 and by -0.003 on one (gate 0.006). Not wanted: `--vision off` on launch, or `--vision no` in setup, leaves the tower out. Checked on Linux (R9700, boston); not on Windows or Strix Halo.
- **More cards get small gains from kernel changes that were measured.** On an RTX PRO 5000 (72 GB, Qwen IQ3_S, five paired runs): story answers 195.9 to 211.8 tok/s (+8.1%), code 240.6 to 244.7 (+1.7%), prompts +1.2% at 4K, +1.5% at 8K, +1.6% at 16K. On two RTX A4000: story +2.2%, code +0.5%. These switches sum numbers in another order, so a reply can differ from 0.2.6 at a near-tie. RTX 40 cards (compute capability 8.9) use measured speed tables for the quantised matrix products; they are bit for bit the same as before and we have no Ada card, so the reporter's measurements are the only ones. Off: `STRATA_MMVQ_IL_89=0`. A100-class cards (sm_80) get the bitwise-identical defaults of #3779 (wider dequantisation, tuned tables, measured only on a CMP 170HX by the contributor); its many opt-ins stay off, and the reporters are asked to test. Off: `STRATA_DEQUANT_WIDE=0`, `STRATA_MMVQ_IL_SM80=0`.
- **The served web chat page gets a large update.** Wide windows use the width and narrow screens fit (#3176). Saved chats with search, rename and delete, editing a question, rewinding to an earlier turn and branching a new chat from it, sending a message while the answer is still coming (wait, send after, or interrupt), math written in LaTeX rendered with KaTeX, a sandboxed preview of HTML and SVG the model writes, and Load and Unload buttons in the header. The chat view is translated into the same languages as the app, French included. The history features are off until you switch them on in Chat settings: with them off the page sends the same requests as before. Monitor, Images and About are still English.
- **The desktop app.** French is the ninth language. Settings now has: a sound when a task finishes (on request), a desktop notification when Manual mode needs your approval, minimise to the system tray, a fixed port so API clients keep working across updates (with a warning when the port is busy), and an interface size up to 200%. The Monitor has a readings strip: power draw, an electricity price you set (in your local currency, found from the system region), disk temperature where Windows or Linux can report it. The DeepSeek card says how much free disk the set needs. Checked in the packaged app on a PC without a screen session: with the port taken, the app starts on the next free port and reports it, and the shell accepts a notification. The tray icon, the pop-up itself and the warning as drawn in the window were not seen on screen.
- **Speed switches.** In Models, Native engine settings, Speed (and in the Terminal's Advanced table): "Faster long prompts" (off by default), "Faster answers on 12 GB NVIDIA cards", "Faster answers on Radeon RX 9000 / AI PRO R9700", "DeepSeek speed-ups". The Terminal also has "Qwen: 0.2.6 behaviour" for troubleshooting.

## Going back to 0.2.6

Two switches bring back every default that 0.2.7 changed, in one step, for a test or for a PC where something looks wrong.

- **`DS4_DEFAULTS=026`** (DeepSeek): the staging ring, the prompt chunk rule, the attention buffer, the pinned copy and the huge-page arena, the matrix-core attention, the drafter's cut, the five-experts default, the RAM store's spare slots and its pre-fill after a prompt, the dense dequantiser, the head and gate/up operand formats and the RDNA3 dense GEMM go back to what 0.2.6 did.
- **`STRATA_DEFAULTS=026`** (Qwen): residency-biased routing, the wide and split hyper-connection reads, the int8 prompt attention, the four gfx12 decode switches, the PLE residency policy, the gfx12 decode split (back to 0.55), the RTX 40 (sm_89) tables, the sm_80 defaults, the layer-major prefill of a two-card CUDA split and the pipelined two-card batch default.

A variable or flag you set yourself still wins over the switch, and the older single switches work as before. In the app, "DeepSeek speed-ups" off sends `DS4_DEFAULTS=026`.

## Off unless you turn it on

- **Faster long prompts** (`STRATA_KVA=1`, or the switch in Models, Native engine settings, Speed). Reads the last 12 layers of a very long prompt in an approximate way, for Qwen3.8-Flash-Next on one NVIDIA or AMD card, on the first read of a prompt of 4,096 tokens or more. On an RTX 5070 with IQ3_S it was 11% faster at 14K and 18% faster at 30K. It stays off because earlier, more aggressive settings dropped records from long lists and failed agent tasks. The setting that ships when you turn it on (layers 36 to 47 approximate, the last 2,048 tokens exact) found the same 585 of 606 facts as the exact read and finished 6 of 10 agent tasks where the exact read finished 4 and 7 in two runs. It can still lose details.
- **Prefill on one card, decode on another** (`--split-serve P,D`, or `split_serve` in the run config; #4000, first version). The idea, the hand-made setup (an RTX 3070 reading the prompt, two MI50 cards making the answer) and the first measurements are by @MarcoTool. One engine reads the prompt and hands the finished state to a second engine that answers. The words are the same as with one engine, token for token (checked at 4,096 and 16,384 tokens, with equal state fingerprints). On two RTX A6000 (3 rounds, 6 values per cell, whole-request time) it was slower than the normal layer split on every workload: an 8K prompt took 16% longer, a 32K prompt 48% longer, a 3-turn chat 30% and 4% longer. So we do not recommend it on two alike cards. It can only pay with two different cards, one good at reading prompts and one good at making answers; we have not measured such a pair. `docs/SPLIT_SERVE.md` has the numbers and the limits.
- **Pipelined drafts for batch slots** (`STRATA_PIPED_MTP=1` with `--batch-mtp`, #4121 by @wannagoxuf). The draft model also runs for the slots of a batch on a two-card layer split. On two RTX A6000 with a batch of slots, five paired runs before the merge: two streams +15.4% (five of five pairs), four streams +4.7%, one stream +0.1%; the merged build, three pairs: +12.2% and +0.2%. Every slot still decodes exactly the tokens it decodes alone (checked slot by slot against a solo run).
- **Huge pages for DeepSeek on Linux.** If you reserve 2 MB huge pages (`vm.nr_hugepages`) big enough for the expert copy, the engine uses them and copies prompt data in place: an 8K prompt on the 2.25 set read 651 tok/s without and 694 with (R9700 limited to 12 GB; that run also set two buffers by hand). Without a reserved pool nothing changes. Not run with a reserved pool on the release package.
- **Settings that help if your PC fits them, no engine change:** `--ple-io ram` (the 28.8 GB table in RAM; on the 72 GB card prompts +16.5% at 1K, +30.6% at 4K, +16.8% at 8K), `--mtp-draft-vocab draft_vocab_en.bin` (+2.7 to +3.1% decode for English text), `--slots 2` for two conversations at once (+10% to +12% aggregate throughput on RTX PRO 5000 and RTX 3060), `--prefill-pipe` on a two-card layer split (+15% at 4K, +23% at 8K prompts on two RTX A4000). `--kv q4_0` on a 12 GB card did not reproduce a gain, so it is a choice, not a default.

## Fixed, from your reports

- Chat: scrolling up while an answer streams works (#4014); a request that timed out shows a badge (#3991).
- The Monitor asks the NVIDIA tool only while it is open or a model runs, which stops the Windows stutter (#4066). The app no longer insists on CUDA when you have a HIP card on Windows (#3892), and the source-checkout host starts an engine with an empty API key (#3851). Deleting a model in the app removes all files of a multi-file model and leaves your own files (#3716).
- The Terminal: `strata launch --set dspark=on` works (#3959); `launch --show-key` knows the config setup wrote (#3570); a model on disk in a differently cased folder is found on Linux instead of being offered for download again (#3996); `--spec 5` can be saved with a warning (#3844).
- Manual mode: read-only commands that have write or execute options now ask first (#3975).
- Engine: a conversation cache no longer reuses another conversation's keys and values (#1503); a short draft-vocabulary row can't be written past (#3911); a checkpoint save that runs out of memory no longer exits the engine (#3350); one cause of the free memory of the second card shrinking with every long cold prompt on a layer split is fixed, a leaked copy stream (#3470, #3350); a hand build for RTX 50 no longer ends up as sm_75 (#4029, #4023); the DeepSeek CUDA packages now include RTX 40 cards (sm_89, #3935); an undeclared tool call returned as text is recovered, declared-only kept (#3796).
- Engine, found by reading the code and the pull requests: a failed read in the per-layer table reader no longer leaves the next request waiting for ever (#3602; the reporter's NaN did not reproduce here, `STRATA_PLE_CHECK=1` re-reads a suspect row and prints it); a conversation restore that would have to create a new copy stream on a card with almost no free memory goes back to the cache instead of failing (#2409); an engine that cannot allocate on a layer split says how much memory it planned to keep free and how much is free (#3638, #3702); the fused int8 tails of `STRATA_QFUSE` used a division that differed from the matrix kernels in about one code per million (#3948, found by a parity test, that switch is off by default, the default path is unchanged); `/v1/responses` accepts -1 and 0 as output limits and reports timings (#4036, #3291); logprobs and allowed token ids on /v1/chat/completions (#3200, partly).
- Opt-in switches from pull requests, each checked for exactness or by unit tests and builds, not for speed on your card: a bigger Pascal (GP100) set (`STRATA_DOWN_WS=1`, `STRATA_MTP_Q8_SM60=1`, `STRATA_MMQ_WS=1`, `STRATA_PATTN_SM60=1`, `STRATA_EXPERT_NIBBLE=1`), `STRATA_PF_FUSED_Q2N=1` for the Q2_0 pack on sm_80 and newer, `STRATA_SELECT_LONG=1` for decoding past 64K cells, `STRATA_VRAM_FREE=device` (Windows, NVML), `STRATA_RAM_ADAPT`, `STRATA_PIPE_ADAPT_EVERY`, `STRATA_SPEC_PROB=1` (a gated draft proposal that keeps the target probabilities, #3416), the sparse copy events on Windows HIP (#4005), and an ARM64 Linux port of the CPU engine whose x86 code compiles to the same objects (#3622, built and cross-compiled, never run on an ARM machine). The speed figures in those pull requests are their authors', not ours.
- Setup: ISTA re-published the first shard of every DeepSeek set on 26 October with a larger chat template; setup refused a copy of it from `--model-path` with "cut short or another version". It accepts it now (by its own size and hash; downloads stay on the pinned revision). The same 0.2.6 setup bug is fixed for people who already have the files.
- Setup and Docker: setup accepts engines that come from the update feed (#4027); a silent re-download in Docker fails loudly (#3421); the Docker image stage carries the scripts the Terminal needs (#3974, #3644); images are tagged 0.2.7.
- Docs: TROUBLESHOOTING is back with every entry that the 0.2.5 rewrite dropped, updated for 0.2.7; the Strix Halo Windows guide (#3029, first written by @HaiYunChuang, measured again here); a Polish README (#3355, by @j-luwierski, the 8th README).
- A graphics card that went through GPU resets can hang engine starts until the PC is rebooted. We saw it on a 4 x R9700 box; 40 loads after a fresh boot had no stall.

Names stay on the commits: 55 contributors' pull requests were ported with their authorship.

## What we did not test

- Prompts longer than a few thousand tokens at 512K or 1M DeepSeek contexts.
- RTX 40 cards (no Ada card here), A100-class cards, RX 6000 on Windows (#3895) and a two-GPU PC with a slow CPU (#3930): shipped from the reporters' measurements; please tell us.
- Whether the new summation orders (RTX PRO and Ampere-class cards) change answers: a 61-task check on the RTX PRO 5000 passed 54 against 55 with the switches off, and its differences stayed inside the spread between two identical runs; it is a small sample.
- Layer-major prefill on cards other than two RTX A4000 (speed) and two RTX A6000 (quality), on Radeon, and on three or more cards; the opt-in switches above on their own hardware.
- DeepSeek pictures on Windows, on Strix Halo and on NVIDIA cards other than the boston A6000 pair.
- The huge-page path with a reserved pool on the release package.
- The DeepSeek Strix Halo package on a 64 GB or 32 GB machine, and the 2.25 set on it.
- The route prior on the owner's RTX 5070: it applies there, and the quality check ran on the RTX 3060.
- The in-app updater from 0.2.6 to 0.2.7 (its files and signatures are checked; we run it after publishing).
- Any Mac beyond the signed build; Metal and SYCL got no 0.2.7 speed change.

## Updating

- **App:** no new installer in 0.2.7.1; the app is still 0.2.7.
- **DGX Spark:** use the install line in the 0.2.7.1 section, then `strata launch`.
- **Terminal:** run `strata update`. From 0.2.6 it fetches Control 0.1.53 and the newer engine in the same run, and keeps the old engine so `strata components rollback` can return to it. From 0.2.7 it fetches Control 0.1.53 only; the engine stays at 0.1.52.
- **DeepSeek engine:** updates itself on the next `strata launch`.

## Downloads

Three installers (Windows, Linux AppImage, Mac dmg) and the Mac updater archive `Strata.app.tar.gz` (all 0.2.7, unchanged), the four Control packages (0.1.53: Windows, Linux x86, Mac, Linux ARM64), the DGX Spark engine and DeepSeek engine packages (0.1.53, `linux-aarch64`), the DeepSeek engine package for the Mac (0.1.53, `macos-arm64-metal`), `strata-feed-linux-aarch64.json` with its signature (the feed that Spark Terminals read), 13 Qwen engine packages and 4 DeepSeek engine packages (all 0.1.52: Windows CUDA 13, Windows AMD for Ryzen AI Max, Linux CUDA 13, Linux AMD rx9070), plus `strata-feed.json` with its signature, `latest.json`, `install-manifest.txt`, `install.sh`, `install.ps1` and `SHA256SUMS.txt`. The DeepSeek CUDA packages are built for sm_86, sm_89 and sm_120.

---

Strata is free and open source. If it runs well on your PC, a coffee keeps the work on it going:

<a href="https://buymeacoffee.com/strataengine"><img src="https://cdn.buymeacoffee.com/buttons/v2/default-yellow.png" alt="Buy Me A Coffee" height="50"></a>

name: Strata 0.2.6
body: # Strata 0.2.6: fixes from the stress tests, a faster DeepSeek on big-RAM PCs, and an uninstaller that finishes the job The app and the Terminal are 0.2.6. The DeepSeek engine and Control are 0.1.51. The Qwen engines stay at 0.1.50: nothing in them changed, so their packages are the same files as in 0.2.5. ## What you will notice - **Uninstalling on Windows removes the program folder.** Strata's own app, host and engine processes are stopped first, so the folder no longer stays behind after you have used the app. This fixes the known issue of 0.2.5. Only processes that run from the install folder are stopped. - **The monitor handles a small integrated graphics chip next to a real card.** With All GPUs, a Radeon or Intel chip inside the CPU is left out of the totals and the count when a real card is present. The hardware report gives each card a stable id, because AMD, Intel and NVIDIA each number their cards from 0. - **About no longer shows the placeholder engine version** (`strata-engine 0.1.0`) while the real one is still being read, and after an engine update it shows the new version, not the old one. - **A DeepSeek model shows its one 8K context on the Models screen**, as in the guided setup, instead of the 32K default. - **A model whose files are all gone is not listed as a download** in Storage and Manage models. - **A chat request with no message is answered with a 400** ("messages must be a non-empty list"), as OpenAI does. A reply of one token shows no tokens-per-second figure; a one-token probe used to read 1,250 tok/s in the monitor. ## DeepSeek is faster on PCs with a lot of RAM When all the CPU-side experts fit in RAM with 8 GiB to spare, the engine now copies all of them in at load and runs without the demand store (all or none, never a part). `--mmap-experts on` or `off`, `--ssd-cache N` and `DS4_STORE_GB` still do what you set. On Windows the check also needs the commit room (RAM plus page file), so a PC with a small page file is not pushed into paging. A PC that cannot hold the whole set, such as a 46 GB RAM PC with a 12 GB card, keeps the store as before and gets the same answers and speed. | Test PC | Set | Decode before | Decode now | |---|---|---|---| | 1 x R9700, 251 GB RAM | 2.00, code | 24.5 tok/s | 27.6 tok/s | | 1 x R9700, 251 GB RAM | 2.00, agent | 21.9 tok/s | 27.1 tok/s | | 1 x R9700, 251 GB RAM | 2.25, code | 26.1 tok/s | 29.6 tok/s | | 1 x R9700, 251 GB RAM | 2.25, agent | 23.1 tok/s | 27.0 tok/s | | 4 x R9700, 251 GB RAM | 2.00, code | 76.6 / 77.0 tok/s | 84.7 / 84.7 tok/s | | 4 x R9700, 251 GB RAM | 2.00, agent | 74.2 tok/s | 83.3 tok/s | Loading takes longer: one R9700 loads the 2.00 set in about 55 s instead of 34 s, because it copies 108 GB. The answers are the same as with `--ssd-cache 0 --mmap-experts off`, which we checked again on the release package. The rule comes from Project Maya (MIT). ## Updating - **App:** the in-app updater installs the new installer. Your engine stays. - **Terminal:** run `strata update`. It fetches Control 0.1.51. Your Qwen engine stays at 0.1.50. - **DeepSeek engine:** updates itself on the next `strata launch` (0.1.50 to 0.1.51). ## AMD in WSL The Linux AMD (HIP) engines hang inside WSL because the GPU bridge there never finishes a command. Setup and `strata launch` now say so and point to the Strata app or Terminal for Windows. They warn and go on; nothing is refused. NVIDIA cards work under WSL as before. ## Small things - Setup no longer stops with "can't reach GitHub" when you point it at a local update feed. - The README and the docs have the new guide set: one installer per system, DeepSeek in the app and the Terminal, and the model order in all seven languages. File names in them are the 0.2.6 ones. ## Downloads Three installers, the three Control packages (0.1.51), 13 Qwen engine packages (0.1.50, unchanged), 3 DeepSeek engine packages (0.1.51: Windows CUDA 13, Linux CUDA 13, Linux AMD rx9070), plus `strata-feed.json` with its signature, `latest.json`, `install-manifest.txt`, `install.sh`, `install.ps1` and `SHA256SUMS.txt`. --- Strata is free and open source. If it runs well on your PC, a coffee keeps the work on it going:

name: Strata 0.2.5
body: # Strata 0.2.5: one installer, DeepSeek in the app, a faster DeepSeek, and a long list of fixes The app and the Terminal are 0.2.5. Every engine package (Qwen and DeepSeek) and the Control are 0.1.50, rebuilt for this release. ## What is new - **One installer per system.** Windows: `Strata-0.2.5-windows-x64-setup.exe`. Linux: `Strata-0.2.5-linux-x86_64.AppImage`. Mac: `Strata-0.2.5-macos-arm64.dmg`. The Windows and Linux files no longer carry an engine. On first start the app shows the engine for your graphics card with its size and one Download button, with progress and resume. If you downloaded the engine file yourself, choose "I already have the file" and it installs offline. The Mac file keeps its small Metal engine inside. - **DeepSeek V4.1-Flash in the app.** The model picker lists the three official sizes, with a plain note on size, speed and disk that warns and never blocks. The context is fixed at 8K and there is no calibration step. - **A Speed choice for DeepSeek: Faster or Full quality.** Faster uses 5 of the model's 6 experts per word, a small quality change that is usually not noticeable. It is the default on a PC with 16 GB of graphics memory or less and on PCs whose graphics share the computer's memory (Strix Halo). In the Terminal: `--speed`, `--full-quality` or `--experts N`. It needs DeepSeek engine 0.1.50 or newer; an older engine gets no Speed step and no flag. On an RTX 5070, Faster mode decoded code and agent runs 16% faster. On a Strix Halo it was 11 to 13% faster to decode and 5 to 7% faster on prompts. On an MI325X the quality checks showed no difference from Full quality. ## DeepSeek is faster on many PCs - **The RAM store can hold every expert.** It used to stop at 48 GB. Where the free RAM holds all routed experts, it now keeps all of them (one R9700 with 251 GB of RAM: 12.6 to 21.4 tokens/s on the 2.00 set). It still leaves 12 GB free. - **The CPU starts on the experts it already has while the rest are read from the SSD.** +13.5% on an RTX 5070 and +11 to 15% on an RTX 3060 PC. - **Fewer GPU launches per layer.** Decode +13% on one test PC in 5 of 5 pairs (same output every run), +2.4% on one R9700 and +4.5% on four. - **Prompt chunk sizes follow what the PC holds.** NVIDIA cards under 16 GB now read prompts in chunks of 4096 instead of 8192: agent decode +2%, an agent turn takes the same time, a cold 8K prompt is 9% slower. AMD cards and cards with 16 GB or more keep 8192. Four R9700 cards that hold most experts use 1024. - **One card on a PC with several cards no longer reads prompts in small chunks.** It used chunks of 1024 and was up to 2 times slower on long prompts (one R9700: 8K prompt 205 to 431 tokens/s). - **Strix Halo.** The prompt kernels use the matrix units on gfx1151: prompts 22% faster at 4K and 29% at 8K, same answers (KL 0.10204 against 0.10203). The RAM store is sized again after the weights are on the GPU, so the PC keeps 12 GB free and 32K and 64K contexts no longer run out of memory on the new AMD driver. - **The same prompt always takes the same path.** The engine now picks the prompt path from the prompt's length (96 tokens and more go through the chunked pass). The old timing guess changed answers between runs. Once the model is ready, the engine also warms up the chunked pass in the background. If a few seconds pass before your first prompt, that prompt no longer pays the one-time setup (about 3.6 s on an R9700). - **Intel server CPUs (Sapphire Rapids and newer) read the i-quant tables with a gather**, which takes 25 to 47% less time on the expert rows we timed (gate and up of one expert, 1 to 4 tokens, on a Xeon 8468; identical output). That is a microbenchmark, not an end-to-end speed. On the AVX-512 CPUs we tested (Zen 4 and Sapphire Rapids), the DeepSeek IQ1_M rows used for prompts are 9% faster, with identical output. - **Qwen engine:** on one CUDA GPU with all experts in RAM, the engine now tries the asynchronous tier itself, measures it for 64 windows and keeps it only if it is not more than 2% slower. ## Fixes in the Terminal - An NVIDIA driver from 528 to 579 runs the CUDA 12 engine by itself and says so (#3843). A card taken out of the PC no longer decides the engine (#3892). RTX 40 cards (sm_89) take the sm_86 package. - A big model gets a longer start wait by itself: 10 minutes plus about 8 s per GB above 40 GB, at most 30 (#3949, #3459). - `strata update` says "the engine was NOT updated" when it was not (#3653), runs the new engine's test start with a short context (#3842) and keeps the CUDA build that runs on your PC (#3835). The launch summary names the engine log (#3656). - Setup: a Mac with an Intel Python is still an Apple Silicon Mac (#3894); the `--kv fp16` flag from the Docker guide works (#3785); a download that gets no data for two minutes says so (#3567); cmake and Visual Studio 2022 are checked in the right order with a plain stop (#3822, #3566); a shared Windows/Linux `.venv` installs again (#3634). - Deleting a model removes the files Strata downloaded, even in another models folder (#3716). A file set with the layout of a tested build is used with a notice (#3651, #3777). - AMD cards on Windows show their memory in setup (#3727, PR #3798 by chicco83). `strata connect` scales the compaction point with the server's context (PR #3852 by demetree). - `strata launch` at 80 columns keeps the verdict column. The DeepSeek engine upgrade lines also show on the setup path. ## Fixes in the app - A finished app update is no longer shown as "Interrupted operation"; the update writes its steps to the log and warns if the app came back as the old version. - Copy response and Copy message say Copied or say why not (#3731); a pasted screenshot is read (#3748); typed line breaks and decimals in the sampling fields work (#3720, #3736); PDFs go into the chat folder (#3838); reopening a chat restores its folder (#3754); downloaded models appear in the chat picker (#3814); one newline inside a paragraph is a soft break (#3818). - The monitor no longer starts a cold PowerShell every 3 seconds (#3939), and shows the memory and load of AMD and Intel cards on Windows (#3727, #3836). With All GPUs, a card that cannot report a value is left out and the one that can is named. - The folder picker falls back to typing the path when security software closes it (#3831). The Models page shows a neutral placeholder until the engine answers (#3740) and counts the chosen context in the memory estimate (#3832). - 69 interface strings that had no key now exist in all eight languages (#3479, #3825). Sizes are decimal MB everywhere. - **Known issue:** uninstalling Strata on Windows right after using it can leave its program folder behind. Close Strata first, then uninstall. ## Updating - **App:** the in-app updater installs the new installer (same file as the download). Your engine stays; the first-run card appears only when there is none. - **Terminal:** run `strata update`. It fetches Control 0.1.50 and the engines you use. - **DeepSeek engine:** updates itself on the next `strata launch` (0.1.49.2 to 0.1.50), as in 0.2.4.2. - **Intel Arc on Linux (SYCL):** needs Ubuntu 24.04 or newer (glibc 2.38). ## Downloads New installers (3), the Control packages (3), 13 engine packages and 3 DeepSeek engine packages, all at 0.1.50, plus `strata-feed.json` with its signature, `latest.json`, `install-manifest.txt`, `install.sh`, `install.ps1` and `SHA256SUMS.txt`. The old per-GPU installers are not attached again. --- Strata is free and open source. If it runs well on your PC, a coffee keeps the work on it going:
